subject: Azure marketplace merchant license split & evidence handback
messages:
From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@aegishealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Voss <markus.voss@azuremarketplace.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Azure listing — license split and evidence requirements

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the call earlier. Procurement here at Aegis needs written confirmation of two items before we can onboard the merchant listing in Azure Marketplace:

1) The proposed license / revenue split for the marketplace listing (we need this for our internal billing exhibit).
2) What evidence you will provide to validate entitlements and how frequently (we have to attach this to the reseller agreement).

Also, please confirm whether Redwood can supply the evidence package as aggregated monthly reports or if you require a per-customer delivery. We prefer a monthly bundle to our procurement mailbox.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — the finance committee meets Thursday.

Thanks,
Lara Chen
Senior Procurement Manager
Aegis Health Systems
[Attachment: procurement_requirements.pdf]
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@aegishealth.com>, Markus Voss <markus.voss@azuremarketplace.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Azure listing — license split and evidence requirements

Hi Lara — thanks, and great to meet earlier.

Quick answers up front:
- License / revenue split: Redwood typically offers a 75/25 split in favor of the merchant on private plan marketplace listings where the merchant owns the customer contract and invoicing. For reference, that is 75% to Aegis, 25% to Redwood before marketplace fees. We can provide a worked example with the SOW numbers if helpful.
- Evidence delivery: Redwood can provide an aggregated monthly evidence bundle (CSV + PDF summary) into a secure SharePoint folder and can also push per-customer artifacts on request. The monthly bundle is standard and should satisfy audit needs.

I've attached a draft SOW and an evidence checklist that maps what we can provide by default.

Next steps: Kimberly / Karthik — can you review the proposed 75/25 commercial split and confirm if legal or finance require alternate language for the marketplace exhibit? Lara / Markus — if 75/25 is acceptable, we will prepare the billing exhibit and DocuSign packet this week.

Best,
Jonas
Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: SOW_DRAFT_v3.pdf, Evidence_Checklist.xlsx]
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lara Chen <lara.chen@aegishealth.com>, Markus Voss <markus.voss@azuremarketplace.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 14:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Azure listing — license split and evidence requirements

Jonas / team,

Thanks for the draft. A couple of legal points we should tidy before we lock 75/25 into the exhibit:

- The split must be net of any Azure marketplace transaction fees — call this out explicitly in the billing exhibit language to avoid downstream disputes.
- We prefer the evidence delivery to include a schema for the entitlement CSV (fields, example rows) and a signed HMAC metadata file to ensure integrity. Can Aegis accept a SHA256 HMAC manifest alongside monthly bundles?
- For audit retention, propose 18 months storage for the evidence bundle; if Aegis requires longer we can discuss an add-on.

Karthik, please look at the proposed marketplace warranty carve-outs and the indemnity references — we may need to soften the language for marketplace economies.

Lara — will HMAC manifests be workable for you or do you need alternatives?

Kimberly
Sr. Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@aegishealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Voss <markus.voss@azuremarketplace.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 09:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Azure listing — license split and evidence requirements

Kimberly — thanks, the HMAC manifest is fine from our side; IT will validate quickly. The 18-month retention is acceptable for now.

On commercial split: our finance team pushed back and countered with 80/20 to Aegis. Their rationale is our procurement fees and onboarding costs for private plan governance. They are OK with a 75/25 if Redwood can commit to covering the first-month onboarding fee (estimated $3,500) and a one-time marketplace listing verification work.

Can Redwood confirm whether the $3.5k onboarding fee would be creditable against the first invoice or handled as a separate charge?

Thanks,
Lara
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@aegishealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Voss <markus.voss@azuremarketplace.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2026 15:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Azure listing — license split and evidence requirements

Lara — thanks for the clear note and for surface-level pushback from finance.

Redwood can accept the 75/25 split as proposed and will credit the first-month onboarding fee of $3,500 against Aegis's first invoice (applied as a one-time credit on the invoice generated for the private plan). We will:

- Update the billing exhibit language to show splits net of Azure fees.
- Include a schema + example CSV for entitlement reporting and a SHA256 HMAC manifest with each monthly bundle.
- Retain evidence bundles for 18 months in the secure SharePoint; access will be granted to Aegis procurement mailbox only.

I have asked Marissa to prepare the updated SOW/billing exhibit and the DocuSign envelope. Marissa — can you get the packet ready for signature today so Aegis can route to your finance team and send to their committee?

Marissa Cole
Manager, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Azure_Marketplace_GUIDE.pdf]
